assumptions.statement: The existing development backend/test environment is sufficient to run the two-client integration and the two-device journey; no cloud provisioning is needed.
The existing one unique WorkManager `note_sync` pipeline and the existing `attachment_sync` separation remain the only sync executors; M5 adds no second pipeline concept.
Two independent Android device instances can be obtained from the existing bounded project tooling (two ADB-visible emulators, one physical device plus one emulator, or two physical devices).
The A3 refresh-rotation model (single-use, retry-safe, reuse detection) is reused as-is for session validity so that revocation invalidates both access and refresh capability.

data_change.notes: Android Room moves 6 -> 7 by a direct experimental bump (project data is disposable; DEV_DATABASE_RESET_REQUIRED = YES; exportSchema stays false; no migration chain is authored), adding only the local installation/session identity and account lifecycle state M5 needs. On the backend, new Flyway migrations after V4 add the session installation identity and the account lifecycle (state, deletion_requested_at, purge_after); no production compatibility chain is authored.

decisions.rationale: This is a human project-owner decision, not a model choice. Re-asking or reinterpreting it would reopen a frozen decision; consuming it as stated keeps the account lifecycle distinct from the Trash lifecycle (D-06) and from the sync tombstone.
decisions.statement: D-05 = ACCOUNT_DELETE_GRACE_30_DAYS is frozen exactly as approved on 2026-10-07: request enters DELETION_PENDING, access is disabled, all sessions are revoked immediately, no new normal sync write is accepted, purge_after = deletion_requested_at + 30 days under server clock authority, cancellation inside the grace window uses the EXISTING verified credential system and restores ACTIVE without resurrecting purged data, and expiry reaches an explicit deterministic purge boundary.

decisions.rationale: The approved decision makes push a future latency optimization only. Making correctness depend on push would invert the approved posture and would add a forbidden dependency.
decisions.statement: D-11 = NO_PUSH_PROVIDER_IN_A8_CORRECTNESS_PATH is frozen: no FCM, Firebase, Google services or vendor push dependency; correctness stays pull/delta based; any future push must sit behind a provider abstraction; A8 PASS must be possible with PUSH_PROVIDER = NONE.

decisions.rationale: A6 is frozen and closed. Redesigning the conflict policy inside a multi-device milestone would invalidate M3 evidence and reopen a completed milestone.
decisions.statement: M5 consumes the existing A6 conflict semantics unchanged and never redesigns them; it only exercises them under real two-client concurrency.

decisions.rationale: Multi-device correctness is exactly the property under test; a single-object mock would silently downgrade the milestone and produce a false PASS.
decisions.statement: The final M5 journey must use two real, independently addressable Android device instances on one account; backend two-client integration tests never replace it, and an unavailable pair yields A8_DEVICE_PAIR_UNAVAILABLE with no PASS.

decisions.rationale: Sessions must be distinguishable without device fingerprinting or invasive identifiers, and without changing the credential architecture.
decisions.statement: A privacy-bounded installation identity generated and persisted by KeepLab itself is used to distinguish independent installations; IMEI, hardware serial, Android ID as a global tracking identity, advertising ID and phone number are never used.

decisions.rationale: A 30-real-day test is not runnable and a production scheduler is out of scope, so the boundary is proven deterministically against the existing development backend/test environment.
decisions.statement: Purge is a deterministic service boundary exercised with an injected/fake clock; no production scheduler and no cloud infrastructure is built or provisioned in M5.

decisions.rationale: Every needed capability (JWT session auth, Room, WorkManager, Ktor client, Flyway) already exists; a new dependency would enlarge the change set and require a separate human decision.
decisions.statement: No Gradle dependency change is authorized; the existing implementation seams are used, and a genuinely indispensable dependency is STOP = M5_DEPENDENCY_DECISION_REQUIRED.

decisions.rationale: The Contract Guard fails closed on unclassified paths, and a broad prefix would re-authorize frozen areas such as the compiler, the verification layer and the contract packages.
decisions.statement: The authorized write surface is exactly the enumerated M5 backend, Android, report and evidence paths, with no broad prefix; a file genuinely outside it is STOP = M5_SURFACE_BROADENING_REQUIRED.

feature.summary: One milestone that proves and hardens multi-device correctness on a single KeepLab account: independent device/session identities, bidirectional propagation and convergence, the existing A6 conflict semantics under real two-client concurrency, a server session list, per-session revoke with non-destructive remote invalidation, account disable, and the human-approved D-05 30-day deletion grace state machine with a deterministic purge boundary — all with PUSH_PROVIDER = NONE (D-11) and with Room kept as the local source of truth.
feature.title: M5 = A8 multi-device hardening

A production cloud scheduler or any cloud provisioning
Any new Gradle dependency, networking stack or CRDT library

requirements.statement: Two or more independent installations must be able to hold a valid session on ONE KeepLab account, and the session representation must let a user tell them apart without device fingerprinting or invasive identifiers.
A write accepted from one client must become visible to the other client through its own pull, and the reverse must hold too, converging without user intervention.
The A6 conflict rules must be exercised and preserved under real server concurrency: two distinct authenticated clients acting from the same base revision.
Device A must be able to revoke Device B's session without destroying B's local data; B's next authenticated request, refresh or sync must be rejected and B must be able to authenticate again.
Disabling an account must make all of its sessions unusable while leaving the Android local notes intact.
Account deletion must be a deliberate, authenticated act that is strictly distinct from the Trash lifecycle and must follow the human-approved D-05 `ACCOUNT_DELETE_GRACE_30_DAYS` semantics.
A8 correctness must hold with `PUSH_PROVIDER = NONE`, and no push provider may be introduced by this milestone.

The final M5 device journey must run against two independent Android device/app instances on one KeepLab account, and multi-device may never be silently downgraded to a single-object mock and reported PASS.
The contract must authorize only the enumerated M5 surfaces and must not authorize any broad prefix.
M5 must be implemented with the existing implementation seams and must not add a dependency.
Local Room remains the single source of truth for the Android UI and the server remains the only revision/order authority; local data is never silently destroyed or reassigned.
M5 is planned once, implemented fully, and verified once, producing one M5 report.

scope: Freeze D-05 ACCOUNT_DELETE_GRACE_30_DAYS and D-11 NO_PUSH_PROVIDER_IN_A8_CORRECTNESS_PATH as approved
Server session/device/account lifecycle: installation-distinguishing session representation, per-session revoke, account disable, ACTIVE -> DELETION_PENDING -> ACTIVE | PURGED
Android installation/session identity, session-list and revoke UX, non-destructive AUTH_REQUIRED
Two independent Android device/app instances on one KeepLab account for the final journey
Real server concurrency between two independent authenticated clients exercising the existing A6 conflict rules
One combined M5 verification pass and one M5 report

stop_conditions: A required write falls outside the enumerated allowed_paths or targets a forbidden path: STOP, CONTRACT_DEVIATION.
Implementation genuinely requires a file outside the enumerated surface: STOP, M5_SURFACE_BROADENING_REQUIRED.
A genuinely indispensable new dependency is discovered: STOP, M5_DEPENDENCY_DECISION_REQUIRED.
Fewer than two usable independent Android device instances exist and no second isolated emulator instance can be supplied: STOP, A8_DEVICE_PAIR_UNAVAILABLE; M5 is NOT reported PASS.
Any push provider, FCM, Firebase, Google services or vendor push dependency would be required: STOP, D11_VIOLATION.

Satisfying M5 would require redesigning the A6 conflict policy, the A5 retry/outbox policy, the A7 attachment architecture or any frozen decision: STOP, CONTRACT_DEVIATION (frozen decision reopening is forbidden).
Any step would delete, reset or reassign Android local Room data or the durable outbox because of a remote revoke, disable, deletion-pending or purge: STOP, LOCAL_DATA_DESTRUCTION_FORBIDDEN.

Satisfying M5 would require modifying specification/, verification/, evaluation/, orchestration/hermes/bridge/, orchestration/hermes/evaluation_adapter/, HERMES-LOCK.json, .hermes.md, reports/contracts/, or the ~/.hermes profile: STOP, ABSOLUTE_BLOCK_VIOLATION.

verification_intent.fixture_intent: Two independent Android device/app instances on ONE KeepLab account (two ADB-visible emulators, one physical device plus one emulator, or two physical devices), each with its own app process, local Room database, secure/session store, KeepLab-generated installation identity and authenticated session. The backend fixture is the existing development backend/test environment with two independent authenticated clients (distinct sessions and installation identities, same account); no cloud infrastructure is provisioned. The D-05 boundary fixture is an injected/fake server clock, never a 30-real-day wait.
verification_intent.oracle_intent: Deterministic only. Primary oracle: the deterministic backend tests, the deterministic two-client backend integration, the deterministic Android JVM tests, and explicit assertions on the two-device journey (persisted Room/outbox state, server-accepted revision, refused status codes, the fake-clock purge_after arithmetic, and the exact A8 gate values). Screenshots are never the primary oracle; on a device failure the evidence may include a screenshot plus the layout hierarchy, logcat and the failed assertion, read once. PUSH_PROVIDER = NONE and PUSH_REQUIRED_FOR_CORRECTNESS = NO are asserted, not assumed. The engine field records the stack's selector-driven device replay family; the real oracle is the deterministic assertions above. Verification runs once; PASS = STOP, and an unavailable real device pair yields A8_DEVICE_PAIR_UNAVAILABLE rather than a mock PASS.
persistence_checks: after a remote revoke or disable the Device B Room note set is unchanged
after a remote revoke or disable the Device B durable outbox is unchanged
LOCAL_ONLY notes remain local and account-scoped cached notes remain account-scoped and are never reassigned
an account in DELETION_PENDING leaves the Android local notes intact
a purge removes only the server account data and never touches Android local Room data
rotation_checks: a revoked refresh token never rotates into a new valid refresh chain
a retried rotation with the same refresh_request_id still recovers the same result
after in-grace cancellation the account is ACTIVE again and a fresh login or refresh succeeds
search_checks: exactly one session in the session list is flagged as the current installation
the two device instances hold distinct session ids and distinct installation identities on the same account
a concurrent write from the same base revision is answered with the authoritative 409 body and no silent overwrite
